[Str6219] † עָשׁוֺת adj. smooth ?—only ´בַּרְוֶל ע Ez 27:19 as merchandise of Tyre; Co עָשׁוּת, i.e. pt. pass., from √ עשׁת forge, or walk skilfully; Toy iron skilfilly wrought; all dubious.

title: II עָשַׁת
content:
[Str6245] † II. [עָשַׁת] vb. Hithp. think (Aramaism: BAram. Pt. עֲשִׁית, Targum אִתְעַשַּׁת);—Hithp. Impf. 3 ms. לָנוּ ´יִתְעַשֵּׁת א Jon 1:6 perhaps God will give a thought to us (cf. חשׁב Psalm 40:18).

[Str6248] † עַשְׁתּוּת (van d. H. וֺת-) n.f. thought;—cstr. שַׁאֲָ+נן ´ע Jb 12:5 (וֺת- would be pl., fr. …עֶ֫שֶׁת).

[Str6250] † [עֶשְׁתֹּנָה] n.f. id. (Aram.: SyrVer עֶשְׁתּוֺנִין; cstr. עשׁתוני Ecclus 3:24);—pl. sf. אָֽבְדוּ עֶשְׁתֹּנֹתָיו Psalm 146:4.

— [עֶשְׁתֹּנָה]: < [עֶשְׁתּוֺן] Margolis (privately).

[Str6249] † עַשְׁתֵּי:19 n. num. one (As. išten, one; išten ešrit, eleven; Dl:§ 75, TelAm. [iš-]tit, first time; v. Gie ZAW i (1881), 226 Ges§ 97 e Köii. l, 212 and reff.);—only + עָשָר, עֶשְרֵה (q. v.) = eleven, eleventh, Je 1:3, 39:2 = 52:5 = 2 K 25:2, Ez 26:1, 40:49, Zc 1:7, Ex 26:7, 26:8, 36:14, 36:15, Nu 7:72, 29:20 (all P), Dt 1:3, 1 Ch 12:13, 24:12, 25:18, 27:14.

[Str6253,1045] † עַשְׁתֹּ֫רֶת n.pr.deae. ‘Aštōreth, < ‘Aštārt, ‘Aštêreth (v. infr.) (MI17 עשתר כמש; Ph. עשתרת (+ oft. in n.pr.), n.pr. עבד עשתר CookAcad. Jan.18, 1896 Sab. n. pr. dei עתַתר v. esp. OsZMG xx (1866), 279 f. DHMib. xxxvii (1883), 376 FellSab. Gotternamen, ZMG liv (1900), 231 ff., esp. 237 ff.; As Isûtar; OAram. Palm. עתר (= עתַתר) in n. pr.; in Egypt. ‘astirati WMMAs. u. Eur. 313; Gk. ‘ Αστάρτη; on their Gk. equivalents (e.g. ï Αφροδίτη) cf. LewyFremdw. 148, 186 f, 250);——ֶֹ prob. artificial, to suggest בּשֶׁת, orig. תַּרְתְּ-, תֶּרֶת-, cf. Isûtar, Ασταρτη, etc.; ´ע 1 K 11:5 + 2 t.; pl. תָּרוֺת- Ju 2:13 + 3t.+ רֹת- 1 S 7:4; 1 S 31:10 rd. prob. sg. (Dr al.);—‘Aštart, ‘Aštereth (Ασταρτη, pl. Ασταρται, but Ju 10:6, 1 S 7:4 Ασταρωθ), ancient Sem. goddess (with male counterpart in Moab., Sab. and appar. Ph.); Phoenician deity, עשׁתרת אֱלֽהֵי צִדֹנִים 1 K 11:5, 11:33, ´שִׁקֻּץ צ ´ע 2 K 23:13; so prob. ´בֵּית ע 1 S 31:10 (rdg. sg.; v. esp. Dr); elsewhere pl., of various local goddesses, called עֲשְׁתָּרוֺת (cf. As. ilâni u ištarat = gods and Ištars (i.e. goddesses), usu. + (ים)בעל, as Canaanitish deities Ju 2:13, 10:6, 1 S 7:4, 12:10; ‖אֱלֽהֵי הַנֵּכָר 7:3.—Vid. esp. DrAshtoreth in HastDB; on Iîitar JastrRel. Bab. pass. esp. 202 f.; on ‘Athtar BaeRel. 117 f; on Ph. on ‘Aštart PietschmGesch. Phön. 184 f.; on ‘Ashtoreth BartonJBL x (1891), 73 ff. GFMEncy. Bib.

[Str1045] I. עַשְׁתָּרוֺת v. foregoing.

[Str6251] † II. [עַשְׁתָּרוֺת] n.pl.f. only cstr. in phr. ת צאֶֹ +נְ(וֺ)עַשְׁתְּר Dt 7:13, 28:4, 28:18, 28:51 (all ‖שְׁגַר אֲלָפֶיְ) usu. interpr. either as a. = ewes (Thes) or as b. = young (cf. veneres gregis; in either case with ref. to ‘Aštart as goddess of fecundity; RS Sem. i. 292, 457 f., 2nd ed. 310, 476 f., adopting b, thinks one type of ‘Ašt in Canaan had form of sheep, so DrDt 7, 13); cf. also عَثَّرِى as name of land fertilized by dew and rain WeSkizzen iii. 170.

[Str6252,6255] † III. עַשְׁתָּרוֺת n.pr.loc. Ασταρωθ, etc., E. of Jordan (name from worship of diff. forms of ‘Aštart; in Egypt. ‘astiratu, as E. Jordan loc. WMMAs. u. Eur. 162, 313; cf. TelAm. n.pr.loc. Aštarti);—in Bashan (near Edrei) Dt 1:4 (רֹת-), Jos 12:4, 13:12, 13:31 (all + אֶדְרֶ֫עִי), 9:10, 1 Ch 6:56 = בְּעֶשְׁתְּרָה (i.e. בֵּית עַשְׁתָּרָה) Jos 21:27; also עַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם Gn 14:5 (LXX Ασταρωθ Καρναιν, cf. GFMJBL xvi(1897), 155 f. who expl. name as Ashtereth of the two-peaked mt:); cf. further, קַרְנַיִם Am 6:13; md; site prob. either Tel ‘ Aštara, 21 miles E. of Sea of Galilee, or Muzeirib, 8 miles further S.; poss. both occur in OT; cf. esp. DrAshtaroth in HastDB DIGn 14, 5), BuhlGeorg. 248 ff. GASmEncy. Bib. 335 f.

[Str6254] † עַשְׁתְּרָתִי adj. gent. of foreg. ´הָע 1 Ch 11:4.

[Str6256] עֵת v. I. ענה

title: I עָתֹד
content:
[Str6257] † I. [עָתֹד] vb. be ready (NH adj. עָתִיד future (as prepared); Ar. عَتُدَ be ready, prepared (also great, bulky); Syr. ܥܬܰܕ, Targum in der. spec. and deriv.);—Pi. Imv. ms. sf. וְעַתְּדָהּ Pr 24:27 and make it ready i. e. thy work (‖הָכֵן).

Hithp. Pf. 3 pl. הִתְעַתְּדוּ לִגַלִּים Jb 15:28 which [houses] were prepared (destined) for (i.e. to be) heaps of ruin.

[Str6259,6264] † עָתִיד, [עָתוּד] adj. ready, prepared;—1. abs. עָתִיד לַכִּידוֺר Jb 15:24 a king ready for the onset; pl. עֲתִדִים לַיּוֺם Est 3:14 ready for the day, so 8:13 Qr (Kt עתודים). 2. ready = skilled הָעֲתִידִים עֹרֵר Jb 3:8 those skilled in rousing Leviathan. 3. prepared = impending (cf. NH= future), fpl. וְחָשׁ עֲתִדֹת Dt 32:35 the impending things are hastening (‖קָרוֺב יוֺם אֵידָם). 4. prepared = stored up, ועתידתיהם Is 10:13 Kt (Qr וַעֲתוּדֹתַיהֶם, to differentiate it from above) and their stores have I plundered.

[Str6260] [עַתּוּד]:29 n.m.:Gn 31:10 he-goat (NH=BH; As. atudû Ar. عَتُودٌ young he-goat; relation to above √ not clear; Thes well-developed, cp. Ar. عَتَدٌ horse fit for running (cf. √ mng. great, i.e. perh. full-grown); acc. to HomNS 247 f. animal ready to fight);—only pl. עַתּוּדִים Is 1:11 + 13 t.; עַתֻּדִים Gn 31:10 + 13 t.; cstr. עַתּוּדֵי Is 34:6; —as property Gn 31:10, 31:12, Ez 27:21, Pr 27:26, food Dt 32:14; as leaders of flock Je 50:8 (sim.), hence fig. of princes and chief men Is 14:9, Ez 34:17, v. also infr.; as sacrif. victims Is 1:11, Nu 7:17 + 12 t. Nu 7, Psalm 66:15 and (iron.) 50:9, 50:13; fig. of people and princes in ´י's great sacrifice Is 34:6, Je 51:40 (sim.), Ez 39:18, and (idea of sacrif. dropped) Zc 10:3.

[Str6258,6261–62] עַתָּה, עַתַּי, עִתִּי v. עֵת sub I. ענהf

[Str6265,5793] † עֲתָיָה n.pr.m. Ne 11:4, Αθεα, LXXL Αθαρασθας (very dub.); = עוּתַי 1 Ch 9:4. p.736

[Str6269,6281] † עֲתָךְ n.pr.loc. in Judah 1 S 30:30 LXXA Αθαγ, LXXL Ναγεβ; HPS prop. עֲרָד; v. עֶתֶר. p. 801

title: עתל
content:
עתל (√ of foll.; perh. = As. atâlu, grow great, cf. etellu, great, exalted; so CheExpos. Times, vii. 484, 568; viii. 48).

[Str6270–71] † (וּ)עֲתַלְיָ֫ה, עַתְלָי n.pr.f. et m. (? ´י is exalted);—1. f. Athaliah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, mother of Ahaziah king of Judah; Γοθολια: יָהוּ- 2 K 8:26, 11:2, 11:20 = 2 Ch 22:2, 22:10, 22:11, 23:12, 23:13, 23:21, 24:7; יָה- 2 K 11:1, 11:3, 11:13, 11:14, 2 Ch 22:12. 2. m. a. 1 Ch 8:26 Ογοθολια. b. Ezr 8:7 Αθελει, A Αθλια; LXXL Γοθονίου (genit.). c. עַתְלָי one with foreign wife Ezr 10:28, Θαλι, A Οθαλι.

title: עָתַם
content:
[Str6272] † [עָתַם] vb. dub.; Niph. Pf. 3 ms. נֶעְתַּם אָרֶץ Is 9:18 (غَتَمَ is be clogged in speech, غَتْمٌ suffocating heat, مَغْتُومٌ burned by heat; hence Thes scorched, but derived sense dub.; v. RSJPhil. xiii. 61 f.);—read perhaps נִצְּתָה (√ יָצַת) is burned up, cf. RSl. c., Krochm Kit CheHpt.

[Str6273] † עָתְנִי n.pr.m Levite 1 Ch 26:7, Γοονει, (Γ)οθνι.

[Str6274] † עָתְנִיאֵל n.pr.m. son of Ḳenaz, a hero in Isr., Γοθονιηλ, Jos 15:17, Ju 1:13, 3:9, 3:11, 1 Ch 4:13, 4:13; name of family 27:15.

title: עָתֵק
content:
[Str6275] † [עָתֵק] vb. move, proceed, advance (NH Hiph.; As. etêku as H., also trans. bring, move; Ar. عَتَقَ, عَتُقَ precede, pass forth, become free, grow old; Aram. ܥܬܶܩ, עֲתַק grow old, Palm. adj. עתק old);—Qal Pf. 3 fs. עָֽתְקָה Psalm 6:8, 3 pl. עָֽתְקוּ Jb 21:7; Impf. 3 ms. יֶעְתַּק Jb 14:18, 18:4; —l. move מִמְּקֹמוֺ ´וְצוּר יֶע Jb 14:18, so 18:4. 2. advance (in years; Aramaic sense) 21:7 (‖יִחְיוּ); hence = grow old and weak Psalm 6:8 (of eye, ‖עָֽשְׁשָׁה). Hiph. Pf. 3 pl. הֶעְתִּיקוּ Jb 32:16 (Gi; van d. H. Baer v15), Pr 25:1; Impf. 3 ms. וַיַּעְתֵּק Gn 12:8, 26:22; Pt. מַעְתִּיק Jb 9:5; —1. move forward (sc. tent) = proceed Gn 12:8 (מִשָּׁם, ה loc.), 26:22 (מִשָּׁם); so fig. Jb 32:16 (v. supr.) words have moved away from them (מֵהֶם), but v. prob. gloss (Bu al.). 2. Jb 9:5 he who removeth mountains. 3. very late Pr 25:1 transcribe (remove from one book or roll to another; LXX ἐξεγράψαντο, Vulgate transtulerunt; so in mediaeval Heb.: ZunzZMG xxv (1871), 447 f. = Ges. Schr. iii. 66 f.).

[Str6277] † עָתָק adj. forward, arrogant (of speech) (Thes free (v. Ar.), unrestrained);—1 S 2:3, Psalm 31:19, 94:4; so also 75:6 (cf. צַוָּאר).

[Str6276] †עָתֵק adj. Thes (ancient and so) valuable; < advanced, eminent, surpassing (cf. عتيق preceding, hence surpassing, choice Lane1947);—´הוֺן ע Pr 8:18 eminent wealth.

[Str6266] † עָתִיק adj. eminent, surpassing, choice (v. עָתֵק);—´מְכַסֶּה ע Is 23:18 choice attire.

[Str6267] † [עַתִּיק] adj. removed, old;—1. removed, עַתִּיקֵי מִשָּׁדָיִם Is 28:9 i.e. weaned (‖גְּמוּלֵי מֵחָלָד; on cstr. v. Ges§ 130 a). 2. old, ancient (Aramaism: עַתִּיק, ܥܰܬܻܝܩ, old), הַדְּדָרִים עַתִּיקִים 1 Ch 4:22.

title: I עָתַר
content:
[Str6279] † I. [עָתַר] vb. pray, supplicafe (always to God) (cf. Ar. عَتَرَ slaughter for sacrifice DeGn (4) 381 We: Skizzen iii. 115, 166; Heid. (2). 118, 142; RS Sem i. 210 f.; 2nd ed.; 227 f.);—Qal Impf. 3 ms. ´וַיֶעְתַּר לי Gn 25:21, ´אֶל־י Ex 8:26, 10:18, Ju 13:8; יֶעְתַּד אֶל־אֱלוֺהַּ Jb 33:26. Niph. be supplicated, entreated (and grant entreaty; always of God), usu. c. ל of worshipper (v. ל 5 d): Pf. 3 ms. consec. וְנֶעְתַּר לָהֶם Is 19:22; Impf. 3 ms. וַיֵּעָ֫תֶר לוֺ Gn 25:21, 2 Ch 33:13, וַיֵּעָתֵר לָנוּ Ezr 8:23; c. לָאָרֶץ for the land 2 S 21:14, 24:25; Inf. abs. לָהֶם וְנַעְתּוֺר 1 Ch 5:20; cstr. (as subst.) הֵעָתֶר־לוֺ 2 Ch 33:19. Hiph. = Qal, make supplication, c. אֶל, לְ: Pf. ´וְהַעְתַּרְתִּ֫י אֶל־י Ex 8:25; Impf. 2 ms. תַּעְתִּיר אֵלָיו Jb 22:27; Imv. mpl. ´הַעְתִּירוּ אֶל־י Ex 8:4, 9:28, ´לי 10:17; also c. ל Pers. in behalf of whom, Impf. 1 S. אַעְתִּיר לְ Ex 8:5, so Imv. חַעְתִּירוּ, c. בַּעֲדִי v:24.

[Str6282] † I. [עָתַר] n.[m.] suppliant, worshipper (?; so usu., but dub.);—only pl. sf. עֲתָרַי Zp 3:10.

title: II עָתַר
content:
[Str6280] II. [עָתַר] vb. be abundant, si Vera l. (as Aram. loan-word; עֲתַר, ܥܬܰܪ, be rich = Heb. עָשַׁר);—Niph. Pt. fpl. נַעְתָּרוֺת Pr 27:6 (of enemy's kisses; De excessive; opp. נֶאֱמָנִים); Toy prop. נֶעֱקָשׁוֺת, or נַעֲוֺת, crooked, hypocritical. Hiph. Pf. 2 mpl. הַעְתַּרְתֶּם עָלַי דִּבְרֵיכֶם Ez 35:13 ye have multiplied against me your words (‖עָלַי בְּפִיכֶם וַתַּגְדִּילוּ), del. as gloss Co after LXX, Toy reads sg., and thinks verb due to Aramaizing scribe.

[Str6283] † עֲתֶ֫רֶת n.f. abundance (Aramaism, si vera l.);—cstr. Je 33:6 I will reveal to them abundance of peace, etc. (corrupt acc. to Gie BuhlLex; Vrss. render variously).

[Str6281,6269] † עֶ֫תֶר n.pr.loc (√ dub.);—in Judah Jos 15:42 ( Ιθακ; A LXXL Αθερ), in Simeon 19:7 (Ιεθερ; in both sq. עָשָׁן); perhaps = עֲתָח q.v.; perhaps (ConderSurvey iii. 261) ‘Atr, c. 2 miles NW. of Beit Jibrin (cf. GASmGeogr., Map).

title: III עתר
content:
III. עתר (√of following)

[Str6282] † II. [עָתָר] n.[m.] odour (si vera l.) (so Vrss.);—cstr. עֲתַר Ez 8:11, of incense.
